import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.10

by A. I. Budkin

Is it true that a quasivariety generated by a finitely generated torsion-free soluble group
and containing a non-abelian free metabelian group, can be defined in the class of
torsion-free groups by an independent system of quasiidentities?

A *quasi-identity* in the language of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n\ \bigl(u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_m = v_m \to u = v\bigr),$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_m, v_m, u, v$ are group words in $x_1, \dots, x_n$ (with $m = 0$
allowed, so identities are quasi-identities). The *quasivariety generated* by a group $G$ is
the smallest quasivariety containing $G$, i.e. the class of all groups satisfying every
quasi-identity that holds in $G$. A system $\Sigma$ of quasi-identities *defines* a class
$\mathfrak{K}$ of groups *in the class of torsion-free groups* if $\mathfrak{K}$ consists
exactly of the torsion-free groups satisfying $\Sigma$, and $\Sigma$ is *independent* in the
class of torsion-free groups if no $\sigma \in \Sigma$ is a consequence of
$\Sigma \setminus \{\sigma\}$ in torsion-free groups, i.e. for every $\sigma \in \Sigma$ there
is a torsion-free group satisfying $\Sigma \setminus \{\sigma\}$ but not $\sigma$.

The free metabelian group on a set $X$ is $F/F''$, where $F$ is the free group on $X$ and
$F'' = [[F, F], [F, F]]$ is its second derived subgroup; it is non-abelian exactly when
$|X| \geq 2$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.10»

/-- A group is torsion-free if the identity is its only element of finite order.

Note that Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (injectivity of $x \mapsto x^n$ for all $n \neq 0$) is a
strictly stronger condition for non-abelian groups. -/
def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups: a universal Horn sentence
$\forall x_1 \dots x_n\ (u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_m = v_m \to u = v)$, where
$u_1, v_1, \dots, u_m, v_m, u, v$ are elements of the free group on the $n$ variables
$x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The number $m$ of premises. -/
  numPremises : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_i = v_i$, each given as the pair of words $(u_i, v_i)$. -/
  premise : Fin numPremises → FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, given as the pair of words $(u, v)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

/-- The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `H`: for every assignment `x` of the variables in
`H`, if all premises of `q` evaluate to true equations then so does its conclusion. Words are
evaluated via `FreeGroup.lift x`. -/
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → H,
    (∀ i, FreeGroup.lift x (q.premise i).1 = FreeGroup.lift x (q.premise i).2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/-- The group `H` belongs to the quasivariety generated by the group `G`, i.e. to the smallest
quasivariety containing `G`: every quasi-identity that holds in `G` holds in `H`. -/
def MemQuasivarietyGenerated (G : Type*) [Group G] (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → q.Holds H

/-- The free metabelian group on `ι`: the quotient $F/F''$ of the free group $F$ on `ι` by its
second derived subgroup $F'' = [[F, F], [F, F]]$. -/
abbrev FreeMetabelianGroup (ι : Type*) :=
  FreeGroup ι ⧸ ⁅commutator (FreeGroup ι), commutator (FreeGroup ι)⁆

/-- A set `S` of quasi-identities is independent in the class of torsion-free groups if no
`q ∈ S` is a consequence of `S \ {q}` in torsion-free groups: for every `q ∈ S` there is a
torsion-free group satisfying every member of `S` other than `q` but not satisfying `q`. -/
def IsIndependentInTorsionFree (S : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsTorsionFreeGroup H ∧
    (∀ r ∈ S, r ≠ q → r.Holds H) ∧ ¬ q.Holds H

/-- The quasi-identity $\forall x\ (x^n = 1 \to x = 1)$. -/
def torsionFreeQuasiIdentity (n : ℕ) : QuasiIdentity where
  numVars := 1
  numPremises := 1
  premise _ := (FreeGroup.of 0 ^ n, 1)
  conclusion := (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem torsionFreeQuasiIdentity_holds_iff (n : ℕ) (H : Type*) [Group H] :
    (torsionFreeQuasiIdentity n).Holds H ↔ ∀ g : H, g ^ n = 1 → g = 1 := by
  simp only [QuasiIdentity.Holds, torsionFreeQuasiIdentity, map_pow, map_one,
    FreeGroup.lift_apply_of]
  exact ⟨fun h g hg => h (fun _ => g) (fun _ => hg), fun h x hx => h (x 0) (hx 0)⟩

/-- Torsion-freeness is defined by the quasi-identities $x^n = 1 \to x = 1$, $n \geq 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isTorsionFreeGroup_iff_holds (H : Type*) [Group H] :
    IsTorsionFreeGroup H ↔ ∀ n, 0 < n → (torsionFreeQuasiIdentity n).Holds H := by
  simp only [torsionFreeQuasiIdentity_holds_iff, IsTorsionFreeGroup, isOfFinOrder_iff_pow_eq_one]
  exact ⟨fun h n hn g hg => h g ⟨n, hn, hg⟩, fun h g ⟨n, hn, hg⟩ => h n hn g hg⟩

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isTorsionFreeGroup_of_isMulTorsionFree (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulTorsionFree G] :
    IsTorsionFreeGroup G :=
  fun _ hg => by_contra fun h => not_isOfFinOrder_of_isMulTorsionFree h hg

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem memQuasivarietyGenerated_self (G : Type*) [Group G] : MemQuasivarietyGenerated G G :=
  fun _ h => h

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem memQuasivarietyGenerated_trans {G H K : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] [Group K]
    (hGH : MemQuasivarietyGenerated G H) (hHK : MemQuasivarietyGenerated H K) :
    MemQuasivarietyGenerated G K :=
  fun q hq => hHK q (hGH q hq)

/-- Every group in the quasivariety generated by a torsion-free group is torsion-free. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isTorsionFreeGroup_of_memQuasivarietyGenerated {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H]
    (hG : IsTorsionFreeGroup G) (hH : MemQuasivarietyGenerated G H) : IsTorsionFreeGroup H :=
  (isTorsionFreeGroup_iff_holds H).2 fun n hn =>
    hH _ ((isTorsionFreeGroup_iff_holds G).1 hG n hn)

/--
Is it true that a quasivariety generated by a finitely generated torsion-free soluble group
and containing a non-abelian free metabelian group, can be defined in the class of
torsion-free groups by an independent system of quasiidentities?

That is: for every finitely generated torsion-free soluble group $G$ such that the
quasivariety $\mathbf{q}G$ generated by $G$ contains some non-abelian free metabelian group,
is there a set $\Sigma$ of quasi-identities, independent in the class of torsion-free groups,
such that a torsion-free group belongs to $\mathbf{q}G$ if and only if it satisfies $\Sigma$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.10» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Group.FG G → IsTorsionFreeGroup G → IsSolvable G →
      (∃ ι : Type, ¬ IsMulCommutative (FreeMetabelianGroup ι) ∧
        MemQuasivarietyGenerated G (FreeMetabelianGroup ι)) →
      ∃ S : Set QuasiIdentity, IsIndependentInTorsionFree S ∧
        ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], IsTorsionFreeGroup H →
          (MemQuasivarietyGenerated G H ↔ ∀ q ∈ S, q.Holds H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.10»

modeling_decisions: Torsion-free is `∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1`, deliberately NOT Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (which is strictly stronger for non-abelian groups). A test lemma proves IsMulTorsionFree → IsTorsionFreeGroup.

Quasi-identities are finite Horn sentences with equations u = v between elements of `FreeGroup (Fin n)`; the representation is not syntactically canonical (e.g. reordering premises), but this does not affect existence of an independent basis (duplicates/equivalent formulas would break independence exactly as in the informal setting, and can always be removed).

'Containing a non-abelian free metabelian group' is stated literally as ∃ ι : Type, ¬ IsMulCommutative (FreeMetabelianGroup ι) ∧ FreeMetabelianGroup ι ∈ qvar(G), rather than via 'rank ≥ 2' (equivalent, since F/F'' on ι is non-abelian iff |ι| ≥ 2; also equivalent to rank-2 membership because quasivarieties are subgroup-closed).

Independence is relative to torsion-free groups (semantic consequence modulo the class); the witness group lives in `Type`, which is harmless by downward Löwenheim–Skolem for the countable language.
Soluble = `IsSolvable`, finitely generated = `Group.FG`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.10

by A. I. Budkin

Is it true that a quasivariety generated by a finitely generated torsion-free
soluble group and containing a non-abelian free metabelian group, can be
defined in the class of torsion-free groups by an independent system of
quasiidentities?

A *quasi-identity* (in the language of groups) is a universally quantified
Horn sentence
$$\forall \bar x\; (u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_k(\bar x) = v_k(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)),$$
where the $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are group words. A *quasivariety* is a class of
groups defined by a set of quasi-identities, and the quasivariety
$\mathbf{q}G$ *generated by* a group $G$ is the smallest quasivariety
containing $G$, i.e. the class of all groups satisfying every quasi-identity
that holds in $G$. A set $\Sigma$ of quasi-identities *defines* a class
$\mathcal{M}$ *in the class of torsion-free groups* if $\mathcal{M}$ is
exactly the class of torsion-free groups satisfying $\Sigma$, and $\Sigma$
is *independent* (relative to torsion-free groups) if no member of $\Sigma$
is a consequence of the remaining members within the class of torsion-free
groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Subgroup

namespace Kourovka.«10.10»

/-- A group $G$ is torsion-free if its only element of finite order is the identity.

Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` asks instead that $x \mapsto x^n$ be injective for all $n \neq 0$,
which is strictly stronger for non-abelian groups, so it is not used here. -/
def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups: a universally quantified Horn sentence
$\forall \bar x\; (u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k \to u = v)$, where the
$u_i, v_i, u, v$ are group words in the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$, encoded as elements
of `FreeGroup ℕ`. The finitely many premise equations $u_i = v_i$ are recorded as the finset
`premises` of pairs $(u_i, v_i)$, and the conclusion $u = v$ as the pair `conclusion`.
Identities are the quasi-identities with no premises. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premise equations $u_i = v_i$, as pairs of group words. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion equation $u = v$, as a pair of group words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group `G` satisfies the quasi-identity `q` if for every assignment `f` of the variables
to elements of `G` under which all the premises of `q` hold, the conclusion of `q` holds too. -/
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f p.1 = FreeGroup.lift f p.2) →
    FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.2

/-- The group `H` belongs to the quasivariety $\mathbf{q}G$ generated by the group `G`, i.e. to
the smallest class of groups defined by quasi-identities that contains `G`: every
quasi-identity that holds in `G` holds in `H`. -/
def MemQuasivarietyGeneratedBy (G : Type*) [Group G] (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → q.Holds H

/-- The free metabelian group on the set `α`: the quotient $F/F''$ of the free group $F$ on
`α` by its second derived subgroup. It is non-abelian exactly when `α` has at least two
elements. -/
abbrev FreeMetabelianGroup (α : Type*) : Type _ :=
  FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) 2

/-- A set `S` of quasi-identities is independent relative to the class of torsion-free groups
if no member of `S` is a consequence of the remaining members of `S` within torsion-free
groups: for each `q ∈ S` there is a torsion-free group satisfying all of `S \ {q}` but not
`q`. -/
def IsIndependentInTorsionFree (S : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsTorsionFreeGroup H ∧
    (∀ q' ∈ S \ {q}, q'.Holds H) ∧ ¬ q.Holds H

/--
Is it true that a quasivariety generated by a finitely generated torsion-free soluble group
and containing a non-abelian free metabelian group, can be defined in the class of
torsion-free groups by an independent system of quasiidentities?

That is: let $G$ be a finitely generated torsion-free soluble group such that the
quasivariety $\mathbf{q}G$ generated by $G$ contains a non-abelian free metabelian group.
Does there exist a set $\Sigma$ of quasi-identities such that $\mathbf{q}G$ is exactly the
class of torsion-free groups satisfying $\Sigma$, and $\Sigma$ is independent relative to
the class of torsion-free groups (no member of $\Sigma$ follows from the others within
torsion-free groups)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.10» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G] [IsSolvable G], IsTorsionFreeGroup G →
      (∃ α : Type, ¬ IsMulCommutative (FreeMetabelianGroup α) ∧
        MemQuasivarietyGeneratedBy G (FreeMetabelianGroup α)) →
      ∃ S : Set QuasiIdentity,
        (∀ (H : Type) [Group H], IsTorsionFreeGroup H →
          (MemQuasivarietyGeneratedBy G H ↔ ∀ q ∈ S, q.Holds H)) ∧
        IsIndependentInTorsionFree S := by
  sorry

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem QuasiIdentity.holds_of_subsingleton (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G]
    [Subsingleton G] : q.Holds G :=
  fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- A group in which $x \mapsto x^n$ is injective for every $n \neq 0$ is torsion-free. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isTorsionFreeGroup_of_isMulTorsionFree (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulTorsionFree G] :
    IsTorsionFreeGroup G :=
  fun _ hg => by_contra fun h => not_isOfFinOrder_of_isMulTorsionFree h hg

/-- A group belongs to the quasivariety it generates. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem memQuasivarietyGeneratedBy_self (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    MemQuasivarietyGeneratedBy G G :=
  fun _ h => h

/-- The free metabelian group is metabelian: its second derived subgroup is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem derivedSeries_freeMetabelianGroup_two (α : Type*) :
    derivedSeries (FreeMetabelianGroup α) 2 = ⊥ := by
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)]
  exact QuotientGroup.map_mk'_self (derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) 2)

/-- The free metabelian group is soluble. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSolvable_freeMetabelianGroup (α : Type*) : IsSolvable (FreeMetabelianGroup α) :=
  ⟨⟨2, derivedSeries_freeMetabelianGroup_two α⟩⟩

end Kourovka.«10.10»

'Independent' is read relative to the class of torsion-free groups (as in the decomposition notes and Budkin's usage): for each q ∈ S there is a torsion-free group satisfying S \ {q} but not q. modeling_decisions: The quasivariety generated by G is defined semantically as the class of groups satisfying all quasi-identities true in G (Mal'cev's theorem), rather than as the S P P_u closure of {G}; the two coincide.

Quasi-identities use finitely many variables (Fin n) and finitely many premises (Finset), each of the form w = 1 with w a word in FreeGroup (Fin n); equations u = v are covered via u v⁻¹ = 1. Identities (no premises) are included as quasi-identities, as is standard.

'Independent' is read relative to the class of torsion-free groups (Budkin's notion of an independent basis of quasi-identities in a class M): for each σ ∈ S there is a torsion-free group satisfying S \ {σ} but not σ. Absolute independence (witness allowed to have torsion) would be a weaker condition.

'Containing a non-abelian free metabelian group' is stated as ∃ X : Type, ¬ IsMulCommutative (FreeMetabelianGroup X) ∧ quasiIdentities G ⊆ quasiIdentities (FreeMetabelianGroup X); the free metabelian group of arbitrary rank is allowed, and non-abelian is used literally (equivalent to rank ≥ 2).

Torsion-free is Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree (no nontrivial element of finite order for groups); soluble is IsSolvable; finitely generated is Group.FG. All groups are quantified in universe Type, following the repository's Kourovka files.
A short proven @[category test] lemma (the trivial group satisfies every quasi-identity) is included as basic API for the bespoke definition, per CONTRIBUTING.md.

statement_blocks.kourovka.«10.10»:
/--
Is it true that a quasivariety generated by a finitely generated torsion-free soluble group
and containing a non-abelian free metabelian group, can be defined in the class of
torsion-free groups by an independent system of quasiidentities?

Formally: let $G$ be a finitely generated torsion-free soluble group such that the
quasivariety $\mathbf{q}(G)$ generated by $G$ contains a non-abelian free metabelian group,
that is, `quasiIdentities G ⊆ quasiIdentities (FreeMetabelianGroup X)` for some `X` with
`FreeMetabelianGroup X` non-abelian. Is there a set $\Sigma$ of quasi-identities such that
* a torsion-free group $H$ lies in $\mathbf{q}(G)$ if and only if $H$ satisfies $\Sigma$, and
* $\Sigma$ is independent in the class of torsion-free groups: for every
  $\sigma \in \Sigma$ there is a torsion-free group satisfying $\Sigma \setminus \{\sigma\}$
  but not $\sigma$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.10» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G] [IsMulTorsionFree G] [IsSolvable G],
      (∃ X : Type, ¬ IsMulCommutative (FreeMetabelianGroup X) ∧
        quasiIdentities G ⊆ quasiIdentities (FreeMetabelianGroup X)) →
      ∃ S : Set QuasiIdentity,
        (∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [IsMulTorsionFree H],
          quasiIdentities G ⊆ quasiIdentities H ↔ S ⊆ quasiIdentities H) ∧
        (∀ q ∈ S, ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsMulTorsionFree H ∧
          S \ {q} ⊆ quasiIdentities H ∧ q ∉ quasiIdentities H) := by
  sorry
